questions.q: What will happen to the people who were suffering?
questions.a: They will not continue to suffer.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do to the people of Zebulun and Naphtali in the past?
questions.a: Yahweh made the people of Zebulun and Naphtali experience great difficulties.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for Zebulun and Naphtali in the future?
questions.a: Yahweh will make things much better for them; he will make that region glorious.

questions.q: On whom will the light shine?
questions.a: The light will shine on the people who live in a land of deep darkness.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for the nation?
questions.a: Yahweh will make the nation larger and increase its joy.

questions.q: What will Yahweh free the people from?
questions.a: Yahweh will free the people from their heavy burden and from those who were oppressing them.

questions.q: What will happen to the soldiers’ boots and blood-stained garments?
questions.a: They will be burned as fuel for fire.

questions.q: What is the name of the one who will bear the rule on his shoulder?
questions.a: His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and Prince of Peace.

questions.q: How will he rule?
questions.a: He will rule with justice and with righteousness.

questions.q: How long will he rule?
questions.a: He will rule from now until forever.

questions.q: What did the Lord send against Jacob?
questions.a: The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it fell on Israel.

questions.q: What did Israel say in pride and with an arrogant heart?
questions.a: Israel said, “The bricks have fallen, but we will build with hewn stone. Sycamores have been cut down, but we will change them into cedars.”

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh raise up against Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh raised up the enemies of Rezin, and he stirred up the Arameans and the Philistines against Israel.

questions.q: After all this did Yahweh’s anger subside?
questions.a: No, Yahweh’s anger did not subside. His hand was still stretched out to strike Israel.

questions.q: Did the people turn to Yahweh?
questions.a: The people did not turn to Yahweh or seek him.

questions.q: Who were the “head” and “tail” that Yahweh was going to cut off in one day?
questions.a: The elder and the noble man were the head, and the prophet who teaches lies was the tail.

questions.q: What are the leaders of the people doing?
questions.a: The leaders are misleading the people, causing them to suffer greatly.

questions.q: Why did the Lord not have compassion on the orphans and widows?
questions.a: He did not have compassion on them because everyone was godless and did evil, and everyone spoke foolish things.

questions.q: After all this did Yahweh’s anger subside?
questions.a: No, Yahweh’s anger did not subside. His hand was still stretched out to strike Israel.

questions.q: What is wickedness compared to?
questions.a: Wickedness is compared to a fire that burns up briars and thorns and spreads into the forest, sending up smoke.

questions.q: What happened as a result of Yahweh’s overflowing anger?
questions.a: Yahweh caused the land to be scorched and the people to become like fuel for the fire.

questions.q: What will Israelites do to their own relatives?
questions.a: Israelites will attack and kill their own relatives.

questions.q: What will happen between Manasseh, Ephraim, and Judah?
questions.a: Manasseh and Ephraim will attack each other, and together they will attack Judah.

questions.q: After all this did Yahweh’s anger subside?
questions.a: No, Yahweh’s anger did not subside. His hand was still stretched out to strike Israel.

commentary.text: The Son that should be born, and his kingdom. (Is. 9:1-7) The judgments to come upon Israel, and on the enemies of the kingdom of Christ. (Is. 9:8-21)

Is. 9:1-7 The Syrians and Assyrians first ravaged the countries here mentioned, and that region was first favoured by the preaching of Christ. Those that want the gospel, walk in darkness, and in the utmost danger. But when the gospel comes to any place, to any soul, light comes. Let us earnestly pray that it may shine into our hearts, and make us wise unto salvation. The gospel brings joy with it. Those who would have joy, must expect to go through hard work, as the husbandman, before he has the joy of harvest; and hard conflict, as the soldier, before he divides the spoil. The Jews were delivered from the yoke of many oppressors; this was a shadow of the believer's deliverance from the yoke of Satan. The cleansing the souls of believers from the power and pollution of sin, would be by the influence of the Holy Spirit, as purifying fire. These great things for the church, shall be done by the Messiah, Emmanuel. The Child is born; it was certain; and the church, before Christ came in the flesh, benefitted by his undertaking. It is a prophecy of him and of his kingdom, which those that waited for the Consolation of Israel read with pleasure. This Child was born for the benefit of us men, of us sinners, of all believers, from the beginning to the end of the world. Justly is he called Wonderful, for he is both God and man. His love is the wonder of angels and glorified saints. He is the Counsellor, for he knew the counsels of God from eternity; and he gives counsel to men, in which he consults our welfare. He is the Wonderful Counsellor; none teaches like him. He is God, the mighty One. Such is the work of the Mediator, that no less power than that of the mighty God could bring it to pass. He is God, one with the Father. As the Prince of Peace, he reconciles us to God; he is the Giver of peace in the heart and conscience; and when his kingdom is fully established, men shall learn war no more. The government shall be upon him; he shall bear the burden of it. Glorious things are spoken of Christ's government. There is no end to the increase of its peace, for the happiness of its subjects shall last for ever. The exact agreement of this prophecy with the doctrine of the New Testament, shows that Jewish prophets and Christian teachers had the same view of the person and salvation of the Messiah. To what earthly king or kingdom can these words apply? Give then, O Lord, to thy people to know thee by every endearing name, and in every glorious character. Give increase of grace in every heart of thy redeemed upon earth.

Is. 9:8-21 Those are ripening apace for ruin, whose hearts are unhumbled under humbling providences. For that which God designs, in smiting us, is, to turn us to himself; and if this point be not gained by lesser judgments, greater may be expected. The leaders of the people misled them. We have reason to be afraid of those that speak well of us, when we do ill. Wickedness was universal, all were infected with it. They shall be in trouble, and see no way out; and when men's ways displease the Lord, he makes even their friends to be at war with them. God would take away those they thought to have help from. Their rulers were the head. Their false prophets were the tail and the rush, the most despicable. In these civil contests, men preyed on near relations who were as their own flesh. The people turn not to Him who smites them, therefore he continues to smite: for when God judges, he will overcome; and the proudest, stoutest sinner shall either bend or break.
